chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Exile is from one city to another city.
And he said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) had exiled two men from Al-Kufa to Al-Basra.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of exile (nafy) in Shia jurisprudence and what example is given from Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the jurisprudential definition of *al-nafy* (exile) as physical relocation between distinct cities, establishing it as a valid penal measure in Shia fiqh. It anchors this ruling in the Sunnah of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), citing his specific precedent of exiling two individuals from Kufa to Basra, thereby demonstrating the practical application of this punishment by the first Imam.
